chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
"Ghusl suffices in place of wudu (ablution), and what wudu (ablution) is purer than ghusl?"

key_terms.أَطْهَرُ: more purifying or purer in effect
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath that removes major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: minor ritual ablution performed for acts such as salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُجْزِي: is sufficient and fulfills the required duty

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl suffice instead of wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that ghusl is sufficient and takes the place of wudu (ablution). It emphasizes the superior purifying function of ghusl, especially in the context of ritual purity after janabah.
